research_scope: Five full source-free reviews: Bell numbers, two Stirling variants, graph coloring and exponential generating functions.

amendments.review_rationale: Read Bell number B_n as count of partitions of any n-element set into disjoint nonempty blocks, including unique empty partition for n=0.
amendments.reason: Reviewed full independent formulation and existing references; distinguished coefficient/adjacency defining predicates from reusable cardinality, arithmetic and convergence-domain concepts.

references.matching_note: The existing cardinality definition applies to finite n-element sets as well as infinite sets.

references.disposition: Counting all partitions of an n-element set is exactly the defining Bell number B_n; the partition concept is already linked.
Empty set has exactly one partition, the empty family of blocks.

amendments.review_rationale: Read Stirling second-kind numbers by base cases using Kronecker delta and two-term recurrence for positive n,k.
amendments.reason: Reviewed full independent formulation and existing references; distinguished coefficient/adjacency defining predicates from reusable cardinality, arithmetic and convergence-domain concepts.

references.disposition: The recurrence for positive n,k is the defining recursion for these Stirling numbers together with boundary conditions.

references.phrase: boundary values for k=0 or n=0
references.disposition: The Kronecker-delta values fix the initial conditions for the defining Stirling recurrence, not another prerequisite meaning.

references.phrase: Stirling second kind counts block partitions
references.disposition: Recurrence is the combinatorial second-kind convention, not first-kind permutation cycle counts.

amendments.review_rationale: Read coefficient definition of Stirling numbers through expansion of monomial basis x^n in falling factorial basis, with zero-index empty product.
amendments.reason: Reviewed full independent formulation and existing references; distinguished coefficient/adjacency defining predicates from reusable cardinality, arithmetic and convergence-domain concepts.

references.phrase: polynomial basis identity x^n=Σ S(n,k) falling(x,k)
references.disposition: This polynomial identity is the coefficient-based defining characterization of the Stirling numbers; falling factorials are already linked.
Uniqueness of coefficients for the falling-factorial basis is part of why the displayed identity defines S(n,k), not an additional prerequisite term. Source-level proof is not certified here.
These constants are Stirling numbers, not coefficients in powers of (x+y).

amendments.review_rationale: Read proper k-vertex-coloring as function to k color labels with inequality on endpoints of every simple-graph edge, without requiring use of all labels.
amendments.reason: Reviewed full independent formulation and existing references; distinguished coefficient/adjacency defining predicates from reusable cardinality, arithmetic and convergence-domain concepts.

references.phrase: finite set of k color labels
references.context: Discrete mathematics: integer label set {1,2,…,k} for a positive integer k, used as a finite k-element codomain with distinct labels.
references.reason: Finite integer label sets are reusable and distinct from a coloring's edge constraint; audit source convention for k=0 separately.

references.disposition: For every edge {u,v}, requiring c(u)≠c(v) is the defining properness condition of vertex coloring, not an independent assumed object.
A proper k-coloring may employ fewer than k colors.

amendments.review_rationale: Read exponential generating function of a real sequence only on the real convergence domain of its n-factorial-weighted power series, retaining nonnegative indices and convergence.
amendments.reason: Reviewed full independent formulation and existing references; distinguished coefficient/adjacency defining predicates from reusable cardinality, arithmetic and convergence-domain concepts.

references.context: Elementary arithmetic: n!=1·2·…·n for positive integer n, with 0!=1, a finite product in natural numbers.
references.reason: Factorial is a separately reusable arithmetic construction appearing in exponential generating functions.

references.context: Real analysis: convergence domain D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n≥0}c_nz^n converges} of a real power series with coefficients c_n, here c_n=a_n/n!.
references.reason: A power-series convergence domain is independently reusable and should not be identified with the particular exponential generating function on it.

references.disposition: Does not assert entire real line convergence; outside D series does not define real value.
